questions.question: Height of 6 persons J, K, L, M, N and O is compared. Height of K is more than only 3 persons. Height of no two persons is same. Height of J is more than M, N and O. Height of J is not maximum. Height of which person is maximum?
questions.solution:
Given that there are 6 persons: **J, K, L, M, N, and O**.

According to the information provided:

**1. Height of K is more than only 3 persons:**

This means **K** is taller than exactly 3 people. In a ranking from 1 (tallest) to 6 (shortest), **K** must be in the 3rd position.

Order: _ > _ > **K** > _ > _ > _

**2. Height of J is more than M, N, and O:**

This implies **J** is taller than at least 3 individuals (**M, N, and O**).

**3. Height of J is not maximum:**

Since **J** is taller than at least 3 people but is not the tallest, **J** must occupy the 2nd position in the ranking (because the 3rd position is already occupied by **K**).

From the above points, we can determine the top of the order:

Position 1: **L** (The only remaining person)

Position 2: **J**

Position 3: **K**

Positions 4, 5, and 6: **M, N, and O** (in some order)

The final descending order of height is: **L > J > K > (M/N/O)**.

Therefore, **L** is the person with the **maximum height**.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2"**.

questions.question: Which part of the Constitution deals with the official language?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part XVII**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part XVII** of the **Constitution of India** deals with the **Official Language** of the country, encompassing **Articles 343 to 351**.
 
• According to **Article 343**, the official language of the **Union** is **Hindi** written in the **Devanagari script**, although the use of **English** was permitted for official purposes for an initial period of 15 years from the commencement of the Constitution.
 
• The provisions are categorized into four distinct chapters: **Language of the Union** (Articles 343-344), **Regional Languages** (Articles 345-347), **Language of the Supreme Court and High Courts** (Articles 348-349), and **Special Directives** (Articles 350-351).
 
• **Article 351** specifically directs the Union to promote the spread of the **Hindi language** and to develop it so that it may serve as a medium of expression for all the elements of the composite culture of **India**.
 
• The **Official Languages Act of 1963** was subsequently enacted to provide for the continued use of **English** for official purposes of the Union and for use in **Parliament** even after the 15-year period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part XV**:

 
 
• This part pertains to **Elections** and includes **Articles 324 to 329**.
 
• It establishes the **Election Commission of India**, which is responsible for the direction and control of **Parliamentary** and **State Legislative** elections.
 
 
 
• **Part XVI**:
 
 
• It contains **Special Provisions** relating to certain classes, covering **Articles 330 to 342**.
 
• These provisions ensure the representation and protection of interests for **Scheduled Castes**, **Scheduled Tribes**, and other backward classes.
 
 
 
• **Part XVIII**:
 
 
• This section covers **Emergency Provisions** under **Articles 352 to 360**.
 
• It empowers the **President of India** to declare a **National Emergency**, **State Emergency (President’s Rule)**, or **Financial Emergency**.

questions.question: Which physical property remains the same on both Earth and the Moon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mass** is defined as the fundamental measure of the total amount of **matter** contained within a physical body or object.
 
• It is an **intrinsic property** of an object, which means it remains constant regardless of the object's location in the universe, whether it is on **Earth**, the **Moon**, or in a state of **weightlessness** in outer space.
 
• The **SI unit** of mass is the **kilogram (kg)**, and it is measured using a **beam balance**, which compares an unknown mass with a known standard mass.
 
• According to **Newton's laws of motion**, mass is a quantitative measure of **inertia**, representing the resistance offered by an object to any change in its state of rest or uniform motion.
 
• Since the quantity of **atoms** and **molecules** within a solid body does not change when moved from one **gravitational field** to another, the **mass** remains identical on both the **Earth** and the **Moon**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Weight**:

 
 
• Unlike mass, **weight** is a **vector quantity** representing the **gravitational force** acting on an object.
 
• It is calculated by the formula **W = m × g**, where 'm' is mass and 'g' is the **acceleration due to gravity**.
 
• Because the Moon's gravity is roughly **1/6th** (approximately **16.6%**) of Earth's gravity, an object will weigh much less on the Moon than on Earth.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Acceleration**:
 
 
• This refers to the **acceleration** of an object caused by the force of **gravitation**.
 
• On **Earth**, the standard value of 'g' is approximately **9.8 m/s²**, while on the **Moon**, it is only **1.62 m/s²** due to the Moon having a smaller **mass** and **radius**.
 
 
 
• **Pressure**:
 
 
• **Pressure** is defined as the **force** exerted per unit **area** (**P = F/A**).
 
• Since the weight (force) of an object changes depending on the **local gravity**, the pressure it exerts on a surface will also differ between the Earth and the Moon.

questions.question: Who was William Wordsworth's collaborator in the publication of "Lyrical Ballads"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Samuel Taylor Coleridge**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lyrical Ballads**, with a Few Other Poems, is a seminal collection first published in **1798**, marking the official beginning of the **Romantic Movement** in **English Literature**.
 
• The work was a landmark collaboration between **William Wordsworth** and **Samuel Taylor Coleridge**, who sought to break away from the rigid, formal structures of 18th-century **Neoclassical poetry**.
 
• The poets established a unique division of labor: **Wordsworth** aimed to provide a fresh perspective on **ordinary life** and **common incidents**, while **Coleridge** focused on **supernatural** elements and making them appear **psychologically credible**.
 
• **Coleridge's** primary contribution to the 1798 edition was the lengthy and iconic poem **The Rime of the Ancient Mariner**, which stands as a masterpiece of **imagination** and **symbolism**.
 
• In the second edition published in **1800**, **Wordsworth** added a famous **Preface** that outlined their poetic manifesto, advocating for the use of the **language of men** rather than elevated **poetic diction**.
 
• The collection also featured **Wordsworth's** **Lines Composed a Few Miles above Tintern Abbey**, which serves as a foundational text for **Pantheism** and nature-oriented philosophy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samuel Taylor Coleridge**:

 
 
• A founder of the **Romantic Movement** and a member of the **Lake Poets**, he is well known for his prose work **Biographia Literaria**.
 
• His unfinished poems **Kubla Khan** and **Christabel** are celebrated for their **Gothic** atmosphere and exploration of the **subconscious**.
 
 
 
• **Robert Southey**:
 
 
• The third major member of the **Lake Poets** along with Wordsworth and Coleridge, he served as the **Poet Laureate** from 1813 to 1843.
 
 
 
• **Percy Bysshe Shelley**:
 
 
• A **Second-Generation Romantic** poet, he was known for his radical politics and lyrical masterpieces like **Prometheus Unbound** and **Ode to the West Wind**.
 
 
 
• **Lord Byron**:
 
 
• Another **Second-Generation Romantic**, famous for creating the **Byronic Hero** and writing the epic satire **Don Juan**.

questions.question: In which Olympic Games was the present Olympic flag first hoisted?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1920 Summer Olympics**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Olympic flag** was designed and created by **Baron Pierre de Coubertin**, the founder of the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)**, in **1913**.
 
• The flag made its official debut and was first hoisted during the **1920 Summer Olympics**, also known as the **Games of the VII Olympiad**, held in **Antwerp, Belgium**.
 
• Although the flag was presented at the **Olympic Congress** in **Paris** in **1914** to mark the **20th anniversary** of the **Olympic Movement**, the **outbreak of World War I** prevented its use in the cancelled 1916 Games.
 
• The **Antwerp Games** represented a symbolic moment of **global peace** and **unity** following the devastation of the **Great War**, making the introduction of the flag highly significant.
 
• The original flag hoisted in **Antwerp** remained the official flag for the **Summer Games** for **68 years** until it was replaced by a new flag at the **1988 Seoul Olympics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Symbolism of the Olympic Flag:**

 
 
• It features **five interlaced rings** of **blue, yellow, black, green, and red** on a **white background**, representing the **five inhabited continents**: **Africa, the Americas, Asia, Europe, and Oceania**.
 
• **Pierre de Coubertin** chose these colors because every **national flag** in the world at that time contained at least one of these **six colors** (including the white base).
 
 
 
• **1924 Summer Olympics (Paris):**
 
 
• These Games were notable for introducing the **Olympic motto**: **Citius, Altius, Fortius** (Faster, Higher, Stronger).
 
• They also established the tradition of raising **three flags** at the closing ceremony: the **IOC flag**, the **host country flag**, and the **next host country flag**.

questions.question: Which hormone inhibits plant growth and can cause wilting of leaves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abscisic acid**__.

__
 
• **Abscisic acid (ABA)** is a specialized **plant growth inhibitor** that regulates various physiological processes, primarily acting as a **stress hormone**.
 
• It inhibits **plant growth** and metabolism, serving as an antagonist to growth-promoting hormones like **Auxins** and **Gibberellins**.
 
• One of its most significant effects is inducing the **closure of stomata** in the leaf epidermis during water stress; this reduces **transpiration** but also results in the **wilting of leaves**.
 
• ABA is responsible for the **abscission** of leaves, fruits, and flowers by promoting the development of the **abscission layer** at the base of the plant organs.
 
• It plays a vital role in **seed development** and **maturation** by inducing **seed dormancy**, ensuring that seeds do not germinate until environmental conditions are favorable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Auxin**:

 
 
• Primarily synthesized at the **shoot and root tips**, it promotes **cell elongation** and **apical dominance**.
 
• It is involved in **phototropism**, causing the plant to grow toward light sources.
 
 
 
• **Gibberellins**:
 
 
• These hormones promote **stem elongation**, **bolting** (sudden stalk growth), and the breaking of **seed dormancy**.
 
• They are widely used in agriculture to increase the size of fruits like **grapes** and to speed up the **malting process** in the brewing industry.
 
 
 
• **Cytokinin**:
 
 
• Essential for **cell division** (cytokinesis), these hormones are found in high concentrations in regions of rapid growth such as **root apices** and **developing shoots**.
 
• They help delay **leaf senescence** and promote the formation of **chloroplasts**.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly reflects triathlon events?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swim, Cycle, Run**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Triathlon** is an endurance multisport race consisting of three distinct disciplines performed sequentially without a significant break between them.
 
• The standard and internationally recognized sequence for a triathlon is **Swimming**, followed by **Cycling**, and concluding with **Running**. This order is strictly maintained by governing bodies like **World Triathlon**.
 
• The **Swim** leg is placed first primarily for safety reasons; athletes are at their freshest at the start, reducing the risk of **exhaustion-related accidents** or drowning in open water.
 
• The **Cycling** leg follows the swim, allowing athletes to utilize a different set of muscle groups while the heart rate settles into a steady rhythm after the horizontal position of swimming.
 
• The **Run** leg serves as the final segment because it is the most physically taxing on the joints due to high-impact movements, and finishing with a run ensures that athletes can safely cross the **finish line** even if they are heavily fatigued.
 
• Efficiency in these events is often determined by **Transitions**, which are the timed intervals spent changing gear between the sports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transition Phases**:

 
 
• **T1 (Transition 1)**: Occurs between the **Swim** and the **Cycle**, where athletes remove wetsuits and put on helmets and cycling shoes.
 
• **T2 (Transition 2)**: Occurs between the **Cycle** and the **Run**, where athletes switch from cycling shoes to running shoes.
 
 
 
• **Standard Race Distances**:
 
 
• **Olympic/Standard Distance**: Comprises a **1.5 km swim**, a **40 km bike ride**, and a **10 km run**.
 
• **Sprint Distance**: Usually half the Olympic distance, involving a **750 m swim**, **20 km bike**, and **5 km run**.
 
• **Ironman Triathlon**: One of the most difficult one-day sporting events, consisting of a **3.8 km swim**, a **180 km bike**, and a full marathon of **42.2 km**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**: The modern version of the sport is widely attributed to the **San Diego Track Club**, which held the first official triathlon in **1974** at **Mission Bay, California**.

questions.question: In which section of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS), plea bargaining has been made time bound?

• The **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023** (BNSS), which replaces the **Code of Criminal Procedure** (CrPC), has introduced a specific time limit for filing **plea bargaining** applications to ensure efficiency in the judicial process.
 
• Under **Section 290(1)** of the BNSS, an accused person is permitted to file an application for plea bargaining only within a period of **thirty days** from the date of **framing of charges** by the court.
 
• The application must be filed in the court where the offence is pending trial and must include a description of the case and an **affidavit** affirming that the accused has voluntarily opted for this process without any coercion.
 
• This **time-bound** provision is a significant departure from the previous **CrPC** framework, where no such specific restrictive deadline was explicitly mentioned for the submission of the application after charges were framed.
 
• By imposing a 30-day limit, the legislature aims to prevent the use of plea bargaining as a **delaying tactic** during the later stages of a criminal trial, thereby upholding the principle of **speedy justice**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plea Bargaining (Chapter XXII)**

 
 
• **Applicability**: It applies to offences that do not carry a punishment of **death**, **imprisonment for life**, or **imprisonment exceeding seven years**.
 
• **Specific Exclusions**: Plea bargaining is strictly prohibited for offences that affect the **socio-economic conditions** of the country or offences committed against a **woman** or a **child below fourteen years** of age.
 
• **Mutually Satisfactory Disposition**: Under **Section 291**, the court provides time for the prosecution, the victim, and the accused to work out a satisfactory disposition of the case, which may include **compensation** to the victim.
 
• **Finality of Judgment**: The judgment delivered by the court under this chapter is **final** and no appeal lies in any court except via a **Special Leave Petition** under **Article 136** or a Writ Petition under **Articles 226 and 227** of the Constitution of India.

questions.question: The sum of a number and its positive square root is 30. What is the value of the number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the sum is an integer (30), the number must be a **perfect square**.

Check **Option (1)**: If the number is **25**, its **positive square root** is **√25 = 5**.

The sum = **25 + 5 = 30**, which matches the given condition.

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **Number + √(Number) = 30**

Let the required **number** be **x**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/da879725f3f27082e130eaa5396211679e9dcc33aaa3f6fc3286f4bd3da6872d.png] 

According to the problem: **x + √x = 30**

Let **√x = y**, then **x = y²**.

⇒ **y² + y = 30**

⇒ **y² + y − 30 = 0**

Applying **middle-term splitting**:

⇒ **y² + 6y − 5y − 30 = 0**

⇒ **y(y + 6) − 5(y + 6) = 0**

⇒ **(y − 5)(y + 6) = 0**

⇒ **y = 5** or **y = −6**

Since **√x** represents a **positive square root**, we take **y = 5**.

⇒ **x = y² = 5² = 25**

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Quadratic Formula

For any quadratic equation **ax² + bx + c = 0**, the roots are calculated as **x = [−b ± √(b² − 4ac)] ÷ 2a**.

Nature of Roots

The **discriminant** (**D = b² − 4ac**) determines the nature of the roots. If **D > 0**, the roots are real and distinct.

Perfect Square Identification

A **perfect square** is an integer that is the square of another integer. Common examples include **1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36**, etc.

questions.question: If √(18.49) + √(29 + x²) = 19.3, then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Determine **√18.49**: Since 4² = 16 and 4.3² = 18.49, the value is **4.3**.

Isolate the radical: **√(29 + x²)** = 19.3 − 4.3 = **15**.

Square both sides: **29 + x² = 15²** ⇒ 29 + x² = 225.

Solve for **x²**: x² = 225 − 29 = 196.

Find **x**: x = √196 = 14.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

√18.49 + √(29 + x²) = 19.3

**Calculation:**

⇒ First, simplify the **decimal square root**: √18.49 = √(1849/100) = 43/10 = 4.3

⇒ Substitute the value back into the **equation**: 4.3 + √(29 + x²) = 19.3

⇒ Subtract 4.3 from both sides: √(29 + x²) = 19.3 − 4.3

⇒ √(29 + x²) = 15.0

⇒ **Squaring both sides** to eliminate the radical:

⇒ (√(29 + x²))² = 15²

⇒ 29 + x² = 225

⇒ x² = 225 − 29

⇒ x² = 196

⇒ x = √196

⇒ x = 14

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Root of Decimals

To find **√x** where x is a decimal, convert it to a **fraction** (e.g., √0.25 = √(25/100) = 5/10 = 0.5) to simplify the calculation.

Perfect Squares and Estimation

Memorizing **perfect squares** up to 30 helps in identifying roots quickly. For example, knowing 14² = 196 and 15² = 225 allows for rapid solving of **algebraic equations**.

Isolating Radicals

When an equation contains a **square root**, always isolate the radical on one side before squaring to avoid creating complex middle terms (2ab).

Factor out the common multiple 4: 4 × (1 + 2 + 3 + ... + 82).

The number of terms **n = 328 ÷ 4 = 82**.

Apply the **sum of first n natural numbers** formula: 4 × [n(n + 1) ÷ 2].

**∴ The correct answer is 13612.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1b92a8a042296fea8f4c9c9a0f281794230ae3238c1a03e7534064ba8c208e82.png] 

**Formula Used:**

n = [(l − a) ÷ d] + 1

**Calculations:**

⇒ n = [324 ÷ 4] + 1

⇒ n = 81 + 1 = 82

⇒ S₈₂ = (82 ÷ 2) × (4 + 328)

⇒ S₈₂ = 41 × 332

Arithmetic Progression (AP)

A sequence where each term is obtained by adding a constant **common difference (d)** to the previous term. The n-th term is aₙ = a + (n − 1)d.

Sum of n terms

The sum can be calculated using Sₙ = (n ÷ 2)[2a + (n − 1)d] or when the last term is known, Sₙ = (n ÷ 2)(a + l).

Sum of first n natural numbers

The sum of numbers 1 + 2 + 3 + ... + n is given by the formula: Σn = n(n + 1) ÷ 2.

questions.question: One angle of a parallelogram is 95 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of its adjacent angle?

In a **parallelogram**, any two **adjacent angles** are **supplementary**, meaning their sum is always **180°**.

Adjacent angle = 180° − 95° = 85°

**∴ The correct answer is 85°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** One angle of the **parallelogram** = 95°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e51cde1b058b6a820151274024252b0ceb7339a7404bc975a6bdcc96850fc58b.png] 

⇒ Let the given angle be ∠A = 95°.

⇒ Let the **adjacent angle** be ∠B.

⇒ ∠A + ∠B = 180°

⇒ 95° + ∠B = 180°

⇒ ∠B = 180° − 95°

⇒ ∠B = 85°

**∴ The correct answer is 85°.**

Opposite Angles

In a **parallelogram**, the opposite angles are always equal in measure (∠A = ∠C and ∠B = ∠D).

Interior Angle Sum

The sum of all four interior angles of any quadrilateral, including a **parallelogram**, is exactly 360°.

Diagonals Property

The diagonals of a **parallelogram** bisect each other, although they are not necessarily equal in length unless the figure is a rectangle.

Arithmetic Progression (AP) Properties

Sum of First n Odd Numbers

Number of Terms Formula

questions.question: Selling price of an article is Rs. 336. Loss percentage is 30 percent. What is the cost price of the article?

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 480.**

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = (336 × 100) ÷ 70

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 480.**

Profit Percentage Formula

SP when Profit% is given

SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

Marked Price and Discount

SP = Marked Price − Discount. Discount % is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**.

**∴ The correct answer is 45000 students.**

Basic Percentage Formula

The value of a percentage is calculated as: **Value = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Total Base**.

Complementary Percentages

In a system with only two outcomes (like Pass/Fail), the sum of their percentages always equals **100%**.

Unitary Method

If p% represents a value V, then 1% represents V/p. Any other percentage q% can be found by multiplying (V/p) × q.

questions.question: R did 5/8 part of a work on first day. He did 1/3 part of the remaining work on second day. Now the remaining work is 10 units. What is the total work (in units)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Total Work** be 24 units (LCM of 8 and 3).

**First Day** work = 5/8 × 24 = 15 units; **Remaining** = 24 − 15 = 9 units.

**Second Day** work = 1/3 × 9 = 3 units.

**Final Remaining** = 9 − 3 = 6 units.

Ratio 6 units = 10 actual units ⇒ 1 unit = 10/6.

**Total Work** = 24 × (10 ÷ 6) = 40 units.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Work done on **First Day** = 5/8 of total.

Work done on **Second Day** = 1/3 of the **remaining work**.

**Final Remaining Work** = 10 units.

**Formula Used:**

**Remaining Work** = Total Work − Total Work Done

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fc2f6b91a3f9f08f713cbbb681bcc113abb8caf20e345c686693491d6d0620bf.png] 

⇒ Let the **Total Work** be W.

⇒ Work done on **Day 1** = 5/8 × W.

⇒ **Remaining work** after Day 1 = W − (5/8)W = 3/8 × W.

⇒ Work done on **Day 2** = 1/3 × (3/8 × W) = 1/8 × W.

⇒ **Total work done** in two days = 5/8 × W + 1/8 × W = 6/8 × W = 3/4 × W.

⇒ **Final Remaining work** = W − 3/4 × W = 1/4 × W.

⇒ 1/4 × W = 10 units.

• In the passive construction, the object **a cutting-edge software for data analysis** becomes the new subject. Since this subject is **singular**, it is paired with the auxiliary verb **has**.

• The word **been** is mandatory in perfect tense passive conversions to indicate the completed state of the action relative to the subject.

• The original subject **The team** is shifted to the end of the sentence as the **agent**, preceded by the preposition **by**.

• Combining these elements results in: **A cutting-edge software for data analysis has been developed by the team.**

 **Additional Information__**

• Voice Conversion Rules based on Tense:

• **Simple Present**: The passive form uses **is/am/are + V3**. (e.g., **is developed**). This is used for habitual actions or general truths.

• **Simple Past**: The passive form uses **was/were + V3**. (e.g., **was developed**). This indicates an action completed at a specific time in the past.

• **Past Perfect**: The passive form uses **had + been + V3**. (e.g., **had been developed**). This is used for an action completed before another point in the past.

• When converting to **Passive Voice**, the object of the active sentence, **'the crops'**, becomes the new subject of the passive sentence.

• The **Future Perfect** verb form **'will have harvested'** must be changed to its passive equivalent, which is **'will have been harvested'** (will have + been + V3).

• The original subject, **'the farmers'**, is introduced as the agent using the preposition **'by'**, resulting in **'by the farmers'**.

• The time indicator **'By next month'** remains consistent in the sentence to denote that the action will be completed by a specific future point.

• Therefore, the resulting sentence maintains the exact meaning and tense of the original while shifting focus to the entity being acted upon (the crops).

 **Additional Information__**

• **Future Perfect Passive Construction**:

• The general formula for **Future Perfect Passive** is: **Subject (Receiver) + will + have + been + Past Participle (V3) + by + Agent (Doer)**.

• It is used specifically for actions that will have been completed before another point in the future.

• The addition of **'been'** is the critical identifier for the **passive transformation** in perfect tenses.

• **Comparison with other Tense Forms**:

• **Future Simple Passive**: Uses **'will be + V3'** (e.g., 'The crops will be harvested'). This indicates a general future action rather than a completed one.

• **Present Perfect Passive**: Uses **'has/have been + V3'** (e.g., 'The crops have been harvested'), which refers to a completed action in the past with current relevance.

• **Future Continuous**: Generally does not have a commonly used passive form in standard English (avoiding **'will be being'**).

</ul

A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."
"Yes my dear your sister's latest novel set in Venice has received rave reviews," said her mother.

options.text: Yes, my dear your sisters' late novel
Yes my dear, your sister's last novel
Yes, my dear, your sister's latest novel

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Yes, my dear, your sister's latest novel**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence requires proper punctuation for an **interjection** and a **vocative expression**. The word **Yes** is an introductory interjection and must be followed by a **comma** to separate it from the main clause. Hence, statement 3 is correct.
 
• The phrase **my dear** is a term of **direct address** (vocative case). According to standard English grammar rules, a person or group being addressed directly must be set off from the rest of the sentence using **commas**. Since it follows an interjection, it needs a comma both before and after it. Hence, statement 3 is correct.
 
• The use of **sister's** is the correct **singular possessive** form, indicating that the novel belongs to one sister. The apostrophe is placed before the 's' to show ownership by a single entity. Hence, statement 3 is correct.
 
• The term **latest** is the **superlative adjective** used to denote the most recent occurrence in a series. In the context of a **novel**, it implies the most recently published work, which fits the intended meaning of the sentence. Hence, statement 3 is correct.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Word Usage and Nuance**:
 
 
• **Latest vs. Last**: While **last** can mean the most recent, it often implies the final item in a sequence where no more will follow. **Latest** specifically highlights the most current work in an ongoing career.
 
• **Late**: Using **late** would imply the sister is deceased or that the novel was overdue, which changes the **semantic meaning** of the original sentence.
 
• **Sisters'**: This is the **plural possessive** form. It would only be used if the novel was co-written by multiple sisters, which is not suggested by the singular context of the sentence.
 
 
 
• **Punctuation Importance**:
 
 
• Omitting the **comma** after **Yes** or around the **vocative** phrase **my dear** leads to a **run-on** effect that obscures the structure of **direct speech** in **narrative writing**.
 
 
</ul

• The verb **insist** cannot be followed by an **object + to-infinitive** structure (e.g., insist someone to do something).

• The sentence should be corrected to: *'She insisted **on my participating** in the competition'* or *'She insisted **that I participate** in the competition.'*
 
• Therefore, the grammatical error is located in **part 2**.

**Correct Sentence:** *'She insisted **on my participating** in the competition.'*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Insist on:** When we use **insist** with a noun or a gerund, we must use the preposition **on**. Example: *'He insisted **on** a receipt.'*
 
• **Insist that:** When using a clause, **that** is used. Example: *'He insisted **that** he was innocent.'*
 
• **In the competition:** This part is grammatically correct as it correctly identifies the event she is referring to.

• Grammatically, distributive pronouns like **Each**, **Either**, and **Neither** are always treated as **singular subjects**.
 
• According to the rules of **Subject-Verb Agreement**, a singular subject must be accompanied by a **singular verb**.
 
• Therefore, the plural verb **are** must be replaced with the singular verb **is** to make the sentence grammatically correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is **äre**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'Neither of the solutions **is** correct.'*

• **Neither of**: This phrase is followed by a **plural noun** or **plural pronoun** (solutions), but the **verb** remains singular because the focus is on each individual item not being correct.
 
• **Neither...nor**: In a correlative conjunction structure, if two subjects are joined by **nor**, the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. However, when **neither** is used alone as the subject, it is strictly singular.
 
• Other examples: '**Neither** of the candidates **has** arrived yet' (Not 'have').
